raw.description:
Health can’t wait.

Not for symptoms to get worse. Not for a six‑month appointment. Not for a system to catch up. But that’s exactly how healthcare works today. You wait, until you can’t.

Alan exists to end the wait.

Health is a universal right, and we believe this right can only become real when it’s coupled with prevention. We need to stop treating health as something we repair and start treating it as something we build, every day. It’s not solely a question of willpower. It’s the healthcare system itself that needs to work for everyone, in a sustainable way.

So we are building the new standard in prevention insurance. Alan is the first company that integrates insurance, prevention, and care into a single, acclaimed user experience.

We are on an incredible journey to build a global leading company, with a unique culture. We already partner with 40K+ companies of all sizes, serving more than 1M+ members, and have reached €800M+ in ARR.

Prevention as the new norm. That's what we're building with our team of 1000+ people. If it speaks to you: we're hiring across France, Spain, Belgium, and Canada. And beyond.

Disclaimer: We're open to hire Account Executives across our Paris, Bordeaux, Marseille, Lyon, Annecy, Nantes and Biarritz offices.

⭐️ The Enterprise Account Executive job

We’re expanding our Sales team in France and are looking for a ‘full-stack’ Enterprise Sales to engage with prospects and turn them into happy Alan customers. You will join a team that mostly focuses on large or very large companies from Tech, Syntec, HCR, and B2B services, interacting with everyone from HR executives to CEOs.

Why is this segment interesting?

  • Diverse workforce: Mix of 60% cadres / 40% non-cadres, often with subsidiaries or multi-site operations, ranging from highly tech-savvy employees to those requiring digital adoption support.

  • Critical challenges: Multi-stakeholder decision processes involving HRD, CFO, CEO, Payroll, CSE, Legal, Purchasing, Comp & Ben, Accounting, Brokers (creating multiple potential blockers), long sales cycles (multi-year conversations), RFP processes requiring deep audits and product customization, and strong influence from unions/CSE who can co-manage health insurance topics;

  • Company profiles: Flagship companies (widely known brands), groups with standalone entities or subsidiaries, often with focus on employee wellbeing (QVT programs, Great Place to Work), modern company culture, and strategic communication about digitization or employer brand attractiveness;

  • HR priorities: Increasing productivity, obtaining fair and competitive pricing, contributing to employee well-being through customized health plans, simplifying HR processes with digital platforms, and managing change management concerns when implementing new health insurance (biggest fear for large companies)

  • Critical business characteristics: This segment requires breadth & depth of expertise to navigate complex organizations, account-based strategies with Key Account Management approach, early engagement in company roadmaps, face-to-face meetings, co-creation of insurance and digital products (tailored offers considering past results, specific regimes, demographics, payroll system integration), and ability to work through RFPs and with brokers. Sales cycles are volatile with high stakes: 1 deal = 50% of annual target for Enterprise AEs.

Our approach for Enterprise companies positions Alan as a strategic partner in health rather than just an insurance provider, emphasizing our digital platform for fluid UX, customized health plans at fair pricing, and health/well-being services. Success requires leveraging high-level connections, building professional materials, and potentially creating exclusive "Health Clubs" or labels for early adopters.

What will you do with us?

You’ll own the entire sales cycle, from prospecting to closing. In our Enterprise Sales team, you will deal with companies with more than 300 employees, including all CAC40 companies.

At Alan, Account Executives drive deals and close strategic opportunities with prospects. We sometimes handle some customer relationships to ensure the best possible onboarding. You’ll educate prospects, provide inspiring product demos, and onboard key stakeholders, making the transition from prospect to customer seamless.

We expect you to understand and apply the Alan Smart & Soft selling method. This method ensures the prospect experience is an integral part of the overall Alan customer experience—making it pleasant and delightful for everyone. We expect you to be instructive to prospects (Smart), as well as to define the best personalized high-touch strategy that suits best each prospect (Soft).

You’ll also help us grow and improve as a company, challenging us to enhance our product(s), methods, and strategy, and getting involved in initiatives to expand our customer base.

Take a look at this testimonial from Emilie Quellec and watch Julien Plessis, both part of the Enterprise Sales team 👀


⭐ Is it you we’re looking for?

You’ll be a great fit for the Enterprise team at Alan if you:

  • Have at least 8 years of experience in Sales, including at least 2 years managing the whole Enterprise Sales cycle, from prospecting to closing.

  • Have full working proficiency in French (C2 and above) and an advanced level in English.

  • Are highly organized with exceptional follow-up skills;

  • Have empathy and are passionate about understanding and solving prospects' problems;

  • Can influence through persuasion, negotiation, and consensus-building;

  • Have a deep understanding of value drivers in recurring revenue business models;

  • Have a great attitude and ability to collaborate in a small team;

  • Are eager to learn fast and make an impact from day 1;

  • Are based in (or willing to relocate to) Paris, Bordeaux, Marseille, Lyon, Annecy, Nantes or Biarritz.

For this opportunity, we are aiming to hire within the D-F level range.

If you're still wondering whether this could be the best move for you, take a look at this article from Lucie Leflour, our Sales Lead in France.


Everything else is a plus. We care about having a diversity of experiences, profiles and backgrounds in our team.


🙌 Perks & Benefits

At Alan, we believe that being in good health is a basic need, and it starts with our employees. This is why Alaners are provided with a stimulating environment and perks ensuring they are happy, efficient and spend only high-quality time with co-workers.

Therefore, we offer:

  • Fair rewards. Generous equity packages complement your base salary, for permanent contracts only.

  • Flexible office with hybrid setup. Amazing office space at our Paris HQ or sponsored co-working hubs in Bordeaux, Marseille, Lyon, Annecy, Nantes or Biarritz.

  • All the tools you need. Top of the range equipment: Macbook Air, keyboard, laptop stand, monitor, and Bose noise-canceling headphones.

  • Flexible vacation policy and flexible working hours. Organize your time as you wish.

  • Delightful healthcare insurance: Extremely comprehensive health insurance - 100% for you and your children, 90-100% for partners depending on your country (permanent contracts only).

  • Transport. Generous transit benefit

  • Learning & Training opportunities. A highly flexible training policy free books and budget to attend and speak at conferences if the opportunity arises.

  • Personal growth through coaching: At Alan, coaching isn't just a perk - it's core to who we are. Every Alaner is paired with a dedicated coach from day one, who helps maximize their impact, nurture engagement, and navigate Alan's values to develop their full potential. Learn more about our coaching culture.

  • Parental leave. Extended parental leave for all new parents, for permanent contracts only.

Important note: we hire people, not roles.

If you're excited about this opportunity but don't check every box, we'd love to hear from you. Everyone, no matter how underrepresented, should feel free to apply as it can only bring learnings or success.

If you identify yourself as a woman: Did you know that research shows women often apply only when meeting 100% of requirements?

Remember, this is just a guide, not a checklist.

We'll be thrilled to receive your application!

🔖 Check out our About Alan and Career pages, as well as our Medium, blog and Glassdoor page for more info.

⭐️ The Enterprise Account Executive job

We’re expanding our Sales team in France and are looking for a ‘full-stack’ Enterprise Sales to engage with prospects and turn them into happy Alan customers. You will join a team that mostly focuses on large companies from Tech, Syntec, HCR, and B2B services, interacting with everyone from HR executives to CEOs.

Why is this segment interesting?

  • Diverse workforce: Mix of 60% cadres / 40% non-cadres, often with subsidiaries or multi-site operations, ranging from highly tech-savvy employees to those requiring digital adoption support.

  • Critical challenges: Multi-stakeholder decision processes involving HRD, CFO, CEO, Payroll, CSE, Legal, Purchasing, Comp & Ben, Accounting, Brokers (creating multiple potential blockers), long sales cycles (multi-year conversations), RFP processes requiring deep audits and product customization, and strong influence from unions/CSE who can co-manage health insurance topics;

  • Company profiles: Flagship companies (widely known brands), groups with standalone entities or subsidiaries, often with focus on employee wellbeing (QVT programs, Great Place to Work), modern company culture, and strategic communication about digitization or employer brand attractiveness;

  • HR priorities: Increasing productivity, obtaining fair and competitive pricing, contributing to employee well-being through customized health plans, simplifying HR processes with digital platforms, and managing change management concerns when implementing new health insurance (biggest fear for large companies)

  • Critical business characteristics: This segment requires breadth & depth of expertise to navigate complex organizations, account-based strategies with Key Account Management approach, early engagement in company roadmaps, face-to-face meetings, co-creation of insurance and digital products (tailored offers considering past results, specific regimes, demographics, payroll system integration), and ability to work through RFPs and with brokers. Sales cycles are volatile with high stakes: 1 deal = 50% of annual target for Enterprise AEs.

Our approach for Enterprise companies positions Alan as a strategic partner in health rather than just an insurance provider, emphasizing our digital platform for fluid UX, customized health plans at fair pricing, and health/well-being services. Success requires leveraging high-level connections, building professional materials, and potentially creating exclusive "Health Clubs" or labels for early adopters.

What will you do with us?

You’ll own the entire sales cycle, from prospecting to closing. In our Enterprise Sales team, you will deal with companies with more than 300 employees, including all CAC40 companies.

At Alan, Account Executives drive deals and close strategic opportunities with prospects. We sometimes handle some customer relationships to ensure the best possible onboarding. You’ll educate prospects, provide inspiring product demos, and onboard key stakeholders, making the transition from prospect to customer seamless.

We expect you to understand and apply the Alan Smart & Soft selling method. This method ensures the prospect experience is an integral part of the overall Alan customer experience—making it pleasant and delightful for everyone. We expect you to be instructive to prospects (Smart), as well as to define the best personalized high-touch strategy that suits best each prospect (Soft).

You’ll also help us grow and improve as a company, challenging us to enhance our product(s), methods, and strategy, and getting involved in initiatives to expand our customer base.

  • Are highly organized with exceptional follow-up skills;

  • Have empathy and are passionate about understanding and solving prospects' problems;

title: Founding engineer- Mo team (AI Health Companion)
description: 🤖 Who we are We’re building Mo — a health companion for everyone. We’re a small team within Alan, on a mission to redefine the future of care by democratizing access to medical expertise . We are building Mo, an intelligent, empathetic, multimodal LLM-based conversational AI assistant able to prescribe, triage, and proactively follow up on care. Imagine giving every person in the world instant, 24/7 access to personalised medical expertise - through chat, voice, or video. That’s what we are building 🤖. We kicked off the project in 2023, and we have launched Mo to all our french members (1M) in Q1 2026, making it the first safe AI health companion live at scale in Europe. 🚀 What keeps us up at night We’re building a medical agent that works — reliably, safely, and at scale . You’ll work at the intersection of product engineering, ML engineering, and medical expertise . Our mission is to build the most accurate and reliable medical agent in the world , while delivering an outstanding conversational experience . Things we’re working on: 💬 Deliver the most memorable chatting experience — You’ll work on making Mo the obvious choice when it comes to asking a health question. It means having a world-class snappy and delightful chatting experience, blazing fast time to answer, and rich content shared. 🧱 Integrate Mo with Alan services and our healthcare system — You’ll work on integrating Mo with our other services (digital chat with HP, map of physical location of HPs, tailored prevention programs, …) to help members get from words to actions. ➕ Extend our architecture to support the next chapters of Mo — You’ll work on our architecture, and agentic framework, to support Mo’s next needs (get more context, use new skills, be accessible in other countries we operate in) If you’re excited by the idea of building the future of healthcare, this is the team for you - we're at the start of the journey. If you’re curious, here is a paper we published recently. 🎯 Is it you we’re looking for? We’re looking for Product engineers with 3+ years of experience who get excited about building state-of-the-art AI systems and applying them to real-world, high-stakes problems in healthcare . You’ll work at the frontier of LLMs, multi-agent architectures, and human-in-the-loop learning — and see your work deployed in production, helping real people. You’ll implement new capabilities for Mo, working across engineering, data, and medical expertise You'll have deep product ownership over the use cases supported in Mo, making sure we actually help our members get and stay better. You’ll have significant influence on system architecture and code quality You’ll mentor engineers, contribute to our product & engineering culture, and help build the team (including participating in hiring, shaping our interview loops, etc.). You would be a good fit in Mo if most of this sounds like you: Applied background in software engineering and systems architecture Experience with traditional ML, or LLMs, or ML dev ops is a big plus. Product-minded: you want your solutions to be used, and impactful Self-directed, pragmatic, driven, hard working Humble and still willing to grow (no matter your seniority!) Collaborative, enthusiastic about teamwork, learning, and teaching Fluent in English (no need to speak French!) raw.description:
🤖 Who we are

We’re building Mo — a health companion for everyone.

We’re a small team within Alan, on a mission to redefine the future of care by democratizing access to medical expertise. We are building Mo, an intelligent, empathetic, multimodal LLM-based conversational AI assistant able to prescribe, triage, and proactively follow up on care.

Imagine giving every person in the world instant, 24/7 access to personalised medical expertise - through chat, voice, or video. That’s what we are building 🤖.

We kicked off the project in 2023, and we have launched Mo to all our french members (1M) in Q1 2026, making it the first safe AI health companion live at scale in Europe.

🚀 What keeps us up at night

We’re building a medical agent that works — reliably, safely, and at scale.

You’ll work at the intersection of product engineering, ML engineering, and medical expertise. Our mission is to build the most accurate and reliable medical agent in the world, while delivering an outstanding conversational experience. Things we’re working on:

  • 💬 Deliver the most memorable chatting experience — You’ll work on making Mo the obvious choice when it comes to asking a health question. It means having a world-class snappy and delightful chatting experience, blazing fast time to answer, and rich content shared.

  • 🧱 Integrate Mo with Alan services and our healthcare system — You’ll work on integrating Mo with our other services (digital chat with HP, map of physical location of HPs, tailored prevention programs, …) to help members get from words to actions.

  • ➕ Extend our architecture to support the next chapters of Mo — You’ll work on our architecture, and agentic framework, to support Mo’s next needs (get more context, use new skills, be accessible in other countries we operate in)

If you’re excited by the idea of building the future of healthcare, this is the team for you - we're at the start of the journey. If you’re curious, here is a paper we published recently.

🎯 Is it you we’re looking for?

We’re looking for Product engineers with 3+ years of experience who get excited about building state-of-the-art AI systems and applying them to real-world, high-stakes problems in healthcare.

  • You’ll work at the frontier of LLMs, multi-agent architectures, and human-in-the-loop learning — and see your work deployed in production, helping real people.

  • You’ll implement new capabilities for Mo, working across engineering, data, and medical expertise

  • You'll have deep product ownership over the use cases supported in Mo, making sure we actually help our members get and stay better.

  • You’ll have significant influence on system architecture and code quality

  • You’ll mentor engineers, contribute to our product & engineering culture, and help build the team (including participating in hiring, shaping our interview loops, etc.).

You would be a good fit in Mo if most of this sounds like you:

  • Applied background in software engineering and systems architecture

  • Experience with traditional ML, or LLMs, or ML dev ops is a big plus.

  • Product-minded: you want your solutions to be used, and impactful

  • Self-directed, pragmatic, driven, hard working

  • Humble and still willing to grow (no matter your seniority!)

  • Collaborative, enthusiastic about teamwork, learning, and teaching

  • Fluent in English (no need to speak French!)

Ils comprennent les marketing mix models (MMM), qui estiment le retour sur investissement de chaque canal média, ainsi que les modèles de demande et de promotion et les modèles de réponse client. Chaque mise à jour fait bouger les estimations, et la première question des métiers est : pourquoi ont-elles bougé ? Notre équipe a développé une méthode qui y répond de façon exacte pour les modèles bayésiens. Elle répartit le déplacement de toute quantité a posteriori entre des groupes d'observations : semaines, campagnes, régions, segments de clients ou expériences. Volet recherche (environ 3 mois) • Étendre l'attribution à l'apprentissage bayésien en ligne : mises à jour séquentielles, effets variables dans le temps (modèles linéaires dynamiques, filtre de Kalman), oubli des données anciennes. • Distinguer les trois causes d'un déplacement à chaque mise à jour : les nouvelles données, un vrai changement du marché et une erreur dans un flux de données. • Calibrer l'alerte de mise à jour : taux de fausses alertes et délai de détection, sur des données simulées dont la vérité est connue et sur des données publiques, pour le MMM et pour au moins un autre modèle marketing. • Rédiger un article destiné à un public de statistique ou de marketing science. title: Intern AI Researcher: Anomaly Detection for Predictive Maintenance in Distributed Storage
description: About Scality Scality builds data infrastructure software for enterprise AI, cyber resilience, and sovereign control at multi-petabyte to exabyte scale. Its AI Data Infrastructure platform reduces operational burden through AI-powered autonomous operations while aligning the right storage media, performance, and protection to each workload through human-approved lifecycle policies.   Built on CORE5 cyber resilience and open-code principles, Scality software delivers extreme performance, operational simplicity, and sustainable economics.    The world's most demanding enterprises and government organizations depend on Scality to power AI initiatives, defend critical data, and build infrastructure that lasts for decades. Recognized as a leader by Gartner, Scality is where AI remembers, learns, and thinks. F   Follow us on LinkedIn. Visit www.scality.com  and our blog. Context & Motivation A distributed storage cluster continuously emits telemetry at every level, from the platform and S3 service down to each server and disk. A failing disk, server or storage node leaves traces in these multivariate time series, from subtle shifts in a few metrics to system-wide disruption. Detecting and diagnosing these anomalies early is critical for: Predictive maintenance: isolating or replacing a component before it impacts service Faster diagnosis: pointing support engineers to the root cause, not just to an alert Higher availability and durability of customer data This internship is part of a joint research project between Scality and an INRIA research team. The project released SHAD (Scality High-dimensional Anomaly Detection), an open benchmark published at NeurIPS 2026 (Evaluations & Datasets Track). It contains 215 real 171-dimensional time series from Scality RING clusters, annotated for injected disk, server and storage-node failures. SHAD's baselines show the problem is far from solved. No detector handles every failure type, per-dimension attributions find root causes no better than chance, and off-the-shelf LLMs cannot interpret the anomalies. This internship builds on SHAD to close these gaps. raw.title: Intern AI Researcher: Anomaly Detection for Predictive Maintenance in Distributed Storage
raw.description:
About Scality

Scality builds data infrastructure software for enterprise AI, cyber resilience, and sovereign control at multi-petabyte to exabyte scale. Its AI Data Infrastructure platform reduces operational burden through AI-powered autonomous operations while aligning the right storage media, performance, and protection to each workload through human-approved lifecycle policies.
 
Built on CORE5 cyber resilience and open-code principles, Scality software delivers extreme performance, operational simplicity, and sustainable economics. 
 
The world's most demanding enterprises and government organizations depend on Scality to power AI initiatives, defend critical data, and build infrastructure that lasts for decades. Recognized as a leader by Gartner, Scality is where AI remembers, learns, and thinks. F
 
Follow us on LinkedIn. Visit www.scality.com and our blog.

Context & Motivation
A distributed storage cluster continuously emits telemetry at every level, from the platform and S3 service down to each server and disk. A failing disk, server or storage node leaves traces in these multivariate time series, from subtle shifts in a few metrics to system-wide disruption. Detecting and diagnosing these anomalies early is critical for:
  • Predictive maintenance: isolating or replacing a component before it impacts service
  • Faster diagnosis: pointing support engineers to the root cause, not just to an alert
  • Higher availability and durability of customer data
    • This internship is part of a joint research project between Scality and an INRIA research team. The project released SHAD (Scality High-dimensional Anomaly Detection), an open benchmark published at NeurIPS 2026 (Evaluations & Datasets Track). It contains 215 real 171-dimensional time series from Scality RING clusters, annotated for injected disk, server and storage-node failures. SHAD's baselines show the problem is far from solved. No detector handles every failure type, per-dimension attributions find root causes no better than chance, and off-the-shelf LLMs cannot interpret the anomalies. This internship builds on SHAD to close these gaps.

    More details on the project: scality.github.io/shad

    Your Mission
    As part of our R&D team and in close collaboration with INRIA researchers, you will develop AI models that detect, explain and interpret anomalies in storage-cluster telemetry. Your work will include: 
     
    1. State of the Art
    Review the literature and open-source projects on multivariate time series anomaly detection, root-cause attribution and LLM-based interpretation of time series. Also survey recent work on AI agents that automate research and experimentation. Starting points include SHAD and the TSB-AD benchmark. 
     
    2. Anomaly Detection & Diagnosis Models
    Design, train and benchmark models that improve on SHAD's baselines at each stage of the pipeline:
  • Detection that stays accurate across disk, server and storage-node failures (e.g., ensembles, hybrid models, time series foundation models)
  • Explanation: attributing each anomaly to the dimensions that actually cause it
  • Interpretation: turning detections into actionable diagnoses (failure type, criticality, affected component) 
  • Early detection of progressive degradations, the core of predictive maintenance
    •  
    3. Fleets of AI Agents for Research
    Set up and manage fleets of AI agents that run your studies at scale:
  • Design agent workflows that launch experiments, run benchmarks and compare methods
  • Orchestrate and monitor many agents working in parallel
  • Build safeguards for rigor: experiment tracking, reproducibility, independent verification of results
  • Assess what agent-driven research changes in practice: speed, coverage, failure modes
    •  
    4. Evaluation & Validation
    Evaluate every model with rigorous, reproducible protocols. Use them to:
  • Measure each stage with SHAD's metrics (VUS-PR for detection, NDCG for explanation, a questionnaire for interpretation)
    Quantify performance per failure family and scenario
  • Identify which approaches are ready to transfer to production monitoring

    • Expected Outcomes & Valorization
    Depending on results, the work may be valorized through:
     
  • A scientific publication with the Scality and INRIA researchers
  • New methods and baselines contributed to the open-source SHAD benchmark
  • Reusable agent-based research workflows for the R&D team

    • Technical Stack
  • Python (primary language for modeling, experimentation and analysis)
  • PyTorch and scikit-learn (deep learning and classical models)
  • SHAD benchmark (github.com/scality/shad) and TSB-AD (github.com/TheDatumOrg/TSB-AD) for data, detectors and evaluation
  • LLM-based AI agents and their orchestration tooling

    • Candidate Profile
  • Final-year student in a Master's program or Engineering school (Bac+5), in machine learning, data science or computer science
  • Solid foundations in machine learning; experience with time series or anomaly detection is a strong plus
  • Strong interest in LLMs and AI agents, and curiosity for new ways of doing research
  • Good Python skills and hands-on experience with a deep learning framework such as PyTorch
  • Rigorous and critical with experimental results, especially when agents produce them
  • Autonomous and curious, able to communicate results clearly in written and spoken English
  • Interest in distributed systems or storage is a plus, not a prerequisite

    • Work Environment
    You will join a fast-paced, lean AI R&D team. French and English is our primary working language. You will benefit from:
     
  • Mentorship from R&D engineers
  • Close collaboration with INRIA researchers working on time series anomaly detection
  • Access to real telemetry from Scality RING clusters and to the AI agent tooling the team uses for its studies
  • A high-trust environment where your findings will directly influence engineering decisions

    • Why Join Scality?
  • Work on a concrete research problem with real-world industrial impact
  • Build on a benchmark published at NeurIPS and contribute to open research
  • Practice a new way of doing research, with fleets of AI agents as research assistants
  • Be part of a team building infrastructure trusted by Fortune 500 companies
  • Potential to publish research or continue as a full-time engineer after the internship

title: CDI - Senior AI Engineer - Paris
description: <h2>Mission</h2> <p>De nouveaux modèles, ouverts ou fermés, sortent chaque mois : encore faut-il choisir ceux qui sont assez bons pour la production, et le démontrer. Applications et agents s’appuient sur les grands modèles de langage (LLM), et la partie modèle de ces systèmes est entre vos mains. Nos clients s’en servent pour répondre à leurs propres clients, traiter des documents et interroger leurs connaissances.</p> <p>Ce que le modèle voit, la manière dont il retrouve les connaissances, les outils qu’il peut appeler : ces choix vous appartiennent, de même que la mesure de la qualité des réponses. Le modèle retenu doit tenir l’objectif de coût et de qualité.</p> <p><strong>Ce poste est fait pour vous si vous voulez savoir si un système d’IA donne des réponses justes, et pas seulement s’il tourne.</strong></p> <p>Artefact accompagne les plus grandes entreprises du monde dans le déploiement de l’IA : 3 000 AI makers dans plus de 30 pays, plus de 1 000 clients. En France, le département Engineering réunit environ 300 personnes sous la responsabilité du CTO ; vous y rejoignez le chapter AI Applied Engineer, archétype AI Engineer.</p> <p>&nbsp;</p> <h2>Activités et responsabilités</h2> <p>Les Product Engineers construisent l’application autour du modèle ; le comportement du modèle à l’intérieur vous revient. Les Context &amp; Analytics Engineers préparent les connaissances que vos agents retrouvent, et les Platform Engineers exploitent le serving, le harness et l’observabilité sur lesquels vous vous appuyez.</p> <p>Avec l’AI Product Manager et les experts métier du client, une bonne réponse se définit, puis les résultats s’examinent ensemble. La relecture de code entre pairs et l’accompagnement des nouvelles recrues font partie du quotidien.</p> <p><strong>Vos responsabilités :</strong></p> <ul> <li>Construire des applications et des agents LLM : conception du contexte, appel d’outils, workflows multi-étapes.</li> <li>Concevoir la façon dont les agents exploitent les connaissances : requêtes de retrieval, re-ranking, citations.</li> <li>Construire des jeux et des pipelines d’évaluation : réponses de référence, scoring automatisé, relecture par des experts métier.</li> <li>Suivre la qualité des réponses en production et corriger ce qui se dégrade.</li> <li>Choisir les modèles selon la qualité, le coût et la latence ; faire du fine-tuning ou de la distillation sur un modèle plus petit quand le prompting ne suffit pas.</li> <li>Ajouter des garde-fous contre les mauvaises réponses, les fuites de données et le prompt injection.</li> <li>Traiter des documents avec des LLM : extraction, classification, résumés.</li> </ul> <p>&nbsp;</p> <h2>Profil recherché</h2> <p><strong>Les indispensables :</strong></p> <ol> <li>Vous avez construit une application ou un agent qui appelle un LLM, et vous savez expliquer ce qui a fonctionné et ce qui a échoué.</li> <li>Votre code est testé et maintenable.</li> <li>Les coding agents font déjà partie de votre quotidien, et vous vérifiez ce qu’ils produisent.</li> <li>La qualité des sorties d’IA se mesure chez vous avec des jeux de test et des métriques, et vous savez limiter les hallucinations, le prompt injection et les fuites de données.</li> <li>Mettre en production une application LLM et la maintenir (déploiement, monitoring, coût, latence) n’a pas de secret pour vous.</li> <li>Le point de départ, pour vous, est le problème métier plutôt que le modèle ; reconnaître que l’IA n’est pas toujours le bon outil, et l’expliquer à des personnes non techniques, fait partie de votre pratique.</li> </ol> <p><strong>Un plus, pas un prérequis :</strong></p> <ul> <li>Du fine-tuning ou de la distillation de modèles de langage.</li> <li>Une formation en machine learning ou en statistiques, par exemple en data science.</li> <li>Des frameworks ou des protocoles d’agents, comme MCP.</li> <li>Des entrées multimodales : documents, images, voix.</li> <li>Des outils d’observabilité LLM : tracing, suivi des coûts.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Pas besoin de cocher toutes les cases pour postuler</strong> : si vous avez l’essentiel des indispensables et l’envie d’apprendre le reste, parlons-en.</p> <p>&nbsp;</p> <h2>Pourquoi nous rejoindre ?</h2> <p>Dans ce métier, la difficulté est moins de faire parler un modèle que de savoir s’il dit juste. L’AI Engineer répond à cette question par la mesure : jeux de test, évaluations, suivi en production, plutôt que par l’impression d’une démonstration réussie.</p> <p>Nous sommes des AI makers : l’IA se construit avec nos clients, pas seulement pour eux. Leurs enjeux deviennent les nôtres, et nos choix techniques s’expliquent dans le langage du métier. Les positions que nous prenons sont claires ; elles évoluent face aux faits, jamais sous la pression.</p> <p>Notre domaine change tous les mois, et ce rythme nous convient : les nouvelles technologies et les nouveaux secteurs s’apprennent vite, et les habitudes qui ne servent plus s’abandonnent sans regret. Devant un problème difficile, le réflexe est de le découper en étapes vérifiables, avec un haut niveau d’exigence sur le code comme sur les livrables.</p> <p>Quand il manque quelque chose, pour un client ou pour le chapter, nous le construisons. La progression passe par des retours constructifs, par le partage des connaissances, par la demande d’aide sans attendre et par la reconnaissance du travail des autres. Il y a beaucoup à apprendre, et beaucoup à construire.</p> <p>Un counsellor accompagne vos premiers mois. L’onboarding technique ouvre le parcours, suivi d’un premier projet client ; si aucun n’est prêt, les starter kits internes prennent le relais.</p> <p>Le reste s’approfondit sur les projets : évaluation, conception d’agents, adaptation de modèles, avec l’appui de la communauté AI Engineer. À partir de 2027, l’archétype AI Engineer disposera de sa propre grille de compétences et de son propre parcours de formation, en plus du socle commun à tous les AI Applied Engineers (responsabilité en production, bases de la sécurité de l’IA).</p> <p>Plus tard, un rôle transverse devient possible (Project Tech Lead, Pre-sales Engineer, Engineering Manager), tout comme les chapters AI Architect et AI Product Manager.</p> <p>&nbsp;</p> <h2>Processus de recrutement</h2> <p>Le processus demande environ quatre heures, réparties en six étapes dont une seule sur site.</p> <ol> <li><strong>Entretien RH</strong> (45 min, à distance) : parcours, motivations et points pratiques, comme le calendrier et les prétentions salariales.</li> <li><strong>Appel avec le CTO</strong> (15 à 30 min, à distance).</li> <li><strong>Screening technique</strong> (30 min, à distance, avec un membre du chapter AI Applied Engineer) : retour détaillé sur vos projets passés, puis questions techniques et de design de solution.</li> <li><strong>Code review et live coding</strong> (60 min, sur site, avec un membre du chapter) : relecture d’un dépôt de code existant et correction de ses défauts, puis construction d’une nouvelle fonctionnalité avec un coding agent et présentation du résultat.</li> <li><strong>Cas technique</strong> (45 min, à distance, avec un membre du chapter) : cadrage d’un problème métier, proposition d’une solution technique, description de la méthode d’évaluation, puis discussion de vos choix.</li> <li><strong>Entretien final</strong> (30 min, à distance, avec une personne de l’encadrement du département, Engineering Manager ou Director) : reprise des points restés ouverts, choix de l’archétype et du niveau les mieux adaptés à votre profil, et réponses à toutes vos questions.</li> </ol> <p>Selon les étapes, tous les outils d’IA sont autorisés, ou aucun. Lors du live coding, c’est la manière de travailler avec l’assistance de l’IA qui est observée.</p> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>Rémunération&nbsp;</strong>: 53 000€ à 70 000€ brut annuel (fixe) + variable selon expérience et séniorité</p> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p><em>Chez Artefact, nous sommes convaincus que la diversité des parcours, des expériences et des perspectives fait la richesse de nos équipes. Nous nous engageons à offrir un environnement inclusif et des opportunités équitables, où chacune et chacun peut évoluer et exprimer pleinement son potentiel. Nos recrutements reposent sur les compétences, le potentiel et l’adéquation avec le rôle.</em></p> Find more English Speaking Jobs in France on Arbeitnow

La relecture de code entre pairs et l’accompagnement des nouvelles recrues font partie du quotidien.</p> <p><strong>Vos responsabilités :</strong></p> <ul> <li>Construire des applications et des agents LLM : conception du contexte, appel d’outils, workflows multi-étapes.</li> <li>Concevoir la façon dont les agents exploitent les connaissances : requêtes de retrieval, re-ranking, citations.</li> <li>Construire des jeux et des pipelines d’évaluation : réponses de référence, scoring automatisé, relecture par des experts métier.</li> <li>Suivre la qualité des réponses en production et corriger ce qui se dégrade.</li> <li>Choisir les modèles selon la qualité, le coût et la latence ; faire du fine-tuning ou de la distillation sur un modèle plus petit quand le prompting ne suffit pas.</li> <li>Ajouter des garde-fous contre les mauvaises réponses, les fuites de données et le prompt injection.</li> <li>Traiter des documents avec des LLM : extraction, classification, résumés.</li> </ul> <p>&nbsp;</p> <h2>Profil recherché</h2> <p><strong>Les indispensables :</strong></p> <ol> <li>Vous avez construit une application ou un agent qui appelle un LLM, et vous savez expliquer ce qui a fonctionné et ce qui a échoué.</li> <li>Votre code est testé et maintenable.</li> <li>Les coding agents font déjà partie de votre quotidien, et vous vérifiez ce qu’ils produisent.</li> <li>La qualité des sorties d’IA se mesure chez vous avec des jeux de test et des métriques, et vous savez limiter les hallucinations, le prompt injection et les fuites de données.</li> <li>Mettre en production une application LLM et la maintenir (déploiement, monitoring, coût, latence) n’a pas de secret pour vous.</li> <li>Le point de départ, pour vous, est le problème métier plutôt que le modèle ; reconnaître que l’IA n’est pas toujours le bon outil, et l’expliquer à des personnes non techniques, fait partie de votre pratique.</li> </ol> <p><strong>Un plus, pas un prérequis :</strong></p> <ul> <li>Du fine-tuning ou de la distillation de modèles de langage.</li> <li>Une formation en machine learning ou en statistiques, par exemple en data science.</li> <li>Des frameworks ou des protocoles d’agents, comme MCP.</li> <li>Des entrées multimodales : documents, images, voix.</li> <li>Des outils d’observabilité LLM : tracing, suivi des coûts.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Pas besoin de cocher toutes les cases pour postuler</strong> : si vous avez l’essentiel des indispensables et l’envie d’apprendre le reste, parlons-en.</p> <p>&nbsp;</p> <h2>Pourquoi nous rejoindre ?</h2> <p>Dans ce métier, la difficulté est moins de faire parler un modèle que de savoir s’il dit juste. L’AI Engineer répond à cette question par la mesure : jeux de test, évaluations, suivi en production, plutôt que par l’impression d’une démonstration réussie.</p> <p>Nous sommes des AI makers : l’IA se construit avec nos clients, pas seulement pour eux. Leurs enjeux deviennent les nôtres, et nos choix techniques s’expliquent dans le langage du métier. Les positions que nous prenons sont claires ; elles évoluent face aux faits, jamais sous la pression.</p> <p>Notre domaine change tous les mois, et ce rythme nous convient : les nouvelles technologies et les nouveaux secteurs s’apprennent vite, et les habitudes qui ne servent plus s’abandonnent sans regret. Devant un problème difficile, le réflexe est de le découper en étapes vérifiables, avec un haut niveau d’exigence sur le code comme sur les livrables.</p> <p>Quand il manque quelque chose, pour un client ou pour le chapter, nous le construisons. La progression passe par des retours constructifs, par le partage des connaissances, par la demande d’aide sans attendre et par la reconnaissance du travail des autres. Il y a beaucoup à apprendre, et beaucoup à construire.</p> <p>Un counsellor accompagne vos premiers mois. L’onboarding technique ouvre le parcours, suivi d’un premier projet client ; si aucun n’est prêt, les starter kits internes prennent le relais.</p> <p>Le reste s’approfondit sur les projets : évaluation, conception d’agents, adaptation de modèles, avec l’appui de la communauté AI Engineer. À partir de 2027, l’archétype AI Engineer disposera de sa propre grille de compétences et de son propre parcours de formation, en plus du socle commun à tous les AI Applied Engineers (responsabilité en production, bases de la sécurité de l’IA).</p> <p>Plus tard, un rôle transverse devient possible (Project Tech Lead, Pre-sales Engineer, Engineering Manager), tout comme les chapters AI Architect et AI Product Manager.</p> <p>&nbsp;</p> <h2>Processus de recrutement</h2> <p>Le processus demande environ quatre heures, réparties en six étapes dont une seule sur site.</p> <ol> <li><strong>Entretien RH</strong> (45 min, à distance) : parcours, motivations et points pratiques, comme le calendrier et les prétentions salariales.</li> <li><strong>Appel avec le CTO</strong> (15 à 30 min, à distance).</li> <li><strong>Screening technique</strong> (30 min, à distance, avec un membre du chapter AI Applied Engineer) : retour détaillé sur vos projets passés, puis questions techniques et de design de solution.</li> <li><strong>Code review et live coding</strong> (60 min, sur site, avec un membre du chapter) : relecture d’un dépôt de code existant et correction de ses défauts, puis construction d’une nouvelle fonctionnalité avec un coding agent et présentation du résultat.</li> <li><strong>Cas technique</strong> (45 min, à distance, avec un membre du chapter) : cadrage d’un problème métier, proposition d’une solution technique, description de la méthode d’évaluation, puis discussion de vos choix.</li> <li><strong>Entretien final</strong> (30 min, à distance, avec une personne de l’encadrement du département, Engineering Manager ou Director) : reprise des points restés ouverts, choix de l’archétype et du niveau les mieux adaptés à votre profil, et réponses à toutes vos questions.</li> </ol> <p>Selon les étapes, tous les outils d’IA sont autorisés, ou aucun. Lors du live coding, c’est la manière de travailler avec l’assistance de l’IA qui est observée.</p> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>Rémunération&nbsp;</strong>: 66 000€ à 85 000€ brut annuel (fixe) + variable selon expérience et séniorité</p> <p>&nbsp;</p> <p><em>Chez Artefact, nous sommes convaincus que la diversité des parcours, des expériences et des perspectives fait la richesse de nos équipes. Nous nous engageons à offrir un environnement inclusif et des opportunités équitables, où chacune et chacun peut évoluer et exprimer pleinement son potentiel. Nos recrutements reposent sur les compétences, le potentiel et l’adéquation avec le rôle.</em></p> Find more English Speaking Jobs in France on Arbeitnow

title: Senior Embedded Linux Software Engineer
description: <p>Auterion builds a cutting-edge operating system for autonomous robotic systems that empower a diverse range of platforms to perform surveillance, reconnaissance, inspection, mapping and logistics tasks. Our industry-leading software drives the adoption of robotic fleets and is recognized by the U.S. government as the future standard for its drone programs.&nbsp;</p> <p>We are looking for a Senior Embedded Linux Software Engineer taking on tasks within the AuterionOS ecosystem, from writing applications to adding driver support for new peripherals, maintaining system services and optimizing performance on embedded platforms. You will be working closely with:</p> <ul> <li>Linux running on embedded hardware</li> <li>C/C++, Python &amp; Bash codebases</li> <li>Engaged and friendly engineers from across Auterion</li> </ul> <p><strong>Responsibilities</strong></p> <ul> <li>Work within the Board Support team and collaborate with other development teams to build leading-edge products.</li> <li>Add features, solve bugs, write tests and improve the performance of software components running on AuterionOS, Auterion’s custom embedded Linux distribution.</li> <li>Collaborate with engineering and product teams to understand both internal and customer use cases.</li> <li>Propose new software solutions and take ownership of the implementation. Your technical expertise will have a huge impact on bringing Auterion’s drone products to market.</li> <li>Provide expert support (L3) to customers facing technical issues.</li> <li>Write clear and concise internal documentation, in addition to contributing to the public-facing knowledge base.</li> <li>Participate in daily stand-ups, as well as release planning and task prioritization meetings.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Qualifications and Skills</strong></p> <ul> <li>B.Sc./M.Sc. in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or related fields.</li> <li>3+ years of experience writing object-oriented C++ and/or Python code in a professional setting.</li> <li>Extensive experience working with embedded architectures, including cross-compilation, debugging, and performance optimization.</li> <li>Expert Linux skills, with an excellent grasp of command line operations, resource management, systems services and networking.</li> <li>Deep knowledge of the Linux kernel, embedded device drivers, device tree configuration and u-boot.</li> <li>Experience with Debian/Ubuntu-based systems, Debian packaging workflows and managing complex Docker environments.</li> <li>Knowledge of OTA updates (e.g. mender).</li> <li>Proficient in networking concepts across all layers of the OSI model, including connectors, and hardware interfaces, IP addressing, routing protocols, DNS, HTTP/HTTPS, etc.</li> <li>Skilled in using network diagnostic tools (e.g., Wireshark, tcpdump) to identify and resolve network issues.</li> <li>Basic embedded security knowledge, such as secure boot on embedded devices and/or UEFI, boot chain verification.</li> <li>Proven experience with network security protocols (e.g., SSL/TLS, VPNs) and best practices for securing embedded devices, such as secure boot and encryption mechanisms.</li> <li>Basic electrical engineering experience, such as familiarity with schematics and the instrumentation required to debug communication over I2C, SPI, UART, CAN bus.</li> <li>Bonus: Experience with video streaming and MIPI CSI drivers.</li> <li>Bonus: Experience with NVIDIA Jetson platforms and their associated BSP packages.</li> <li>Bonus: Experience with NXP iMX8 platforms and their associated BSP packages.</li> <li>Bonus: Previous contributions to open source projects, especially in the Linux ecosystem.</li> <li>Bonus: Experience with CI/CD systems, such as Jenkins, GitHub actions, GitLab CI.</li> <li>Experience working in an agile environment, providing daily updates in stand-ups and managing tasks in a sprint board.</li> <li>A product-oriented mindset, with an eagerness to drive forward project initiatives.</li> <li>EU Citizenship required.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Benefits</strong></p> <ul> <li>Flexible working hours</li> <li>Stock Options</li> <li>Generous holiday allowance</li> <li>Company pension plan&nbsp;</li> <li>Car parking&nbsp;&nbsp;</li> <li>Enhanced maternity &amp; paternity leave</li> <li>Mental health and wellbeing support</li> <li>Learning and development opportunities</li> </ul> <p><strong>About Auterion</strong></p> <p>We are building the leading software platform for AI-powered autonomous systems for enterprise and government customers. Our team is supporting the most important missions and solving the most challenging problems.</p> <p>At Auterion, we bring together the sharpest minds who love to solve the hardest problems. Join a vibrant team built on innovation, openness, and excellence, where you’ll be empowered to develop ideas, collaborate across all levels, and make an impact that matters.</p> Find Jobs in Switzerland on Arbeitnow

title: Senior Reinforcement Learning Engineer
description: Gravis Robotics is a high-growth Series A start-up backed by SoftBank, bringing Physical AI to the construction industry, turning heavy construction machines into autonomous robots.  Gravis began as an ETH Zurich spin-out, and our unique combination of learning-based automation and augmented remote control lets one operator safely conduct a fleet of earthmoving machines in a gamified environment.    Backed by deep robotics research and now deployed across multiple countries with leading construction and equipment partners, our team is rapidly growing to bring this technology to a trillion-dollar industry.    The Gravis RACK is a machine-agnostic retrofit kit that adds autonomy to excavators and wheel loaders from 10 to 100+ tonnes: LiDAR and camera sensing, GNSS RTK, networking hardware and rugged edge compute that works offline. Paired with the Slate tablet and our Copilot software, it lets an operator run a machine manually, with AI assistance, or fully autonomously.   About the Job   The autonomy team at Gravis builds autonomous systems for excavators operating in real construction environments. You will build control modules that run on many different machines , across many sites, with different soil conditions. We’re looking for a roboticist with data driven planning and/or control background, deep python expertise and good level of C++ proficiency.   To be successful in this role you should have experience working with real robots, tackling the challenges of sim2real transfer, and deploying robotic systems in a production environment.     What you will do Learning-Based Planning and Control for Real Systems   Develop data driven planning and control systems for autonomous excavation that generalize across machine models and soil conditions Contribute to  simulation improvements that reduce or address the sim2real gap Define data collection and curation pipelines for incorporating real data in policy training  Design experiments focused on continuous performance and robustness improvements. Explore the usage of adaptive and online reinforcement learning in deployed systems Provide mentorship and supervision for junior team members, interns, and students.   System Integration   Integrate learned components into a larger software stack Collaborate with excavation and motion planning engineers Build tools for analysing and evaluating the behavior of learned components What we’re looking for We recognize that excellent candidates come from diverse backgrounds with various combinations of skills. If you meet most of the core qualifications below, we highly encourage you to apply. Core qualifications 2–5 years industry experience developing Reinforcement learning systems for control and/or planning and deploying them on real robots with a customer. If you only have experience with simulation, you’re most likely not a good fit for this position. Experience with GPU accelerated simulation environments (e.g. IsaacSim/IsaacLab, CARLA, MuJoCo) Strong Python skills and experience with PyTorch or similar libraries Proficiency in C++ Comfortable debugging real-world system behavior Ability and willingness to travel as required by business projects.  Great-to-Have Skills & Experience Experience with hydraulic machinery Experience with supervised learning or imitation learning Research experience in reinforcement learning Experience deploying robotic systems at scale (e.g. hundreds of units) Familiarity with ROS or similar robotics frameworks Experience with feature-flagged deployments, staged rollouts, or long-lived platforms Experience with data curation for ML applications Experience guiding, mentoring, or leading junior colleagues, students, or project teams.  Familiarity with or interest in utilizing AI coding tools.  This Role is a Great Fit If You are passionate about building systems that work reliably in the real world You want to help build a long-lived excavation planning and control system intended to scale and positively impact the entire construction industry.  You are comfortable working with the realities of imperfect data and noisy measurements. You have a keen interest in bridging the sim2real gap and understanding the differences between simulation and physical environments.  You are excited to help drive technical direction in a growing team transitioning from prototyping to the product stage. You value a collaborative team culture rooted in thoughtful design, creative thinking, mutual respect, and pragmatism.  Don't meet every requirement? If you're enthusiastic about this role but your experience doesn't match every qualification, we still encourage you to apply. You might be the perfect candidate for this or other positions. This is an opportunity to join a dynamic and versatile team, and to be part of a young startup that will revolutionize heavy construction.   Gravis Robotics offers a fair market salary and a working location in the vibrant city of Zurich. raw.title: Senior Reinforcement Learning Engineer
raw.description:
Gravis Robotics is a high-growth Series A start-up backed by SoftBank, bringing Physical AI to the construction industry, turning heavy construction machines into autonomous robots. 

Gravis began as an ETH Zurich spin-out, and our unique combination of learning-based automation and augmented remote control lets one operator safely conduct a fleet of earthmoving machines in a gamified environment. 
 
Backed by deep robotics research and now deployed across multiple countries with leading construction and equipment partners, our team is rapidly growing to bring this technology to a trillion-dollar industry. 
 
The Gravis RACK is a machine-agnostic retrofit kit that adds autonomy to excavators and wheel loaders from 10 to 100+ tonnes: LiDAR and camera sensing, GNSS RTK, networking hardware and rugged edge compute that works offline. Paired with the Slate tablet and our Copilot software, it lets an operator run a machine manually, with AI assistance, or fully autonomously.  

About the Job
 
The autonomy team at Gravis builds autonomous systems for excavators operating in real construction environments. You will build control modules that run on many different machines, across many sites, with different soil conditions. We’re looking for a roboticist with data driven planning and/or control background, deep python expertise and good level of C++ proficiency.
 
To be successful in this role you should have experience working with real robots, tackling the challenges of sim2real transfer, and deploying robotic systems in a production environment.
 
 

What you will do
Learning-Based Planning and Control for Real Systems
 
  • Develop data driven planning and control systems for autonomous excavation that generalize across machine models and soil conditions
  • Contribute to  simulation improvements that reduce or address the sim2real gap
  • Define data collection and curation pipelines for incorporating real data in policy training 
  • Design experiments focused on continuous performance and robustness improvements.
  • Explore the usage of adaptive and online reinforcement learning in deployed systems
  • Provide mentorship and supervision for junior team members, interns, and students.
    •  
    System Integration
     
  • Integrate learned components into a larger software stack
  • Collaborate with excavation and motion planning engineers
  • Build tools for analysing and evaluating the behavior of learned components

    • What we’re looking for

    We recognize that excellent candidates come from diverse backgrounds with various combinations of skills. If you meet most of the core qualifications below, we highly encourage you to apply.

    Core qualifications

  • 2–5 years industry experience developing Reinforcement learning systems for control and/or planning and deploying them on real robots with a customer. If you only have experience with simulation, you’re most likely not a good fit for this position.

  • Experience with GPU accelerated simulation environments (e.g. IsaacSim/IsaacLab, CARLA, MuJoCo)

  • Strong Python skills and experience with PyTorch or similar libraries

  • Proficiency in C++

  • Comfortable debugging real-world system behavior

  • Ability and willingness to travel as required by business projects. 

    • Great-to-Have Skills & Experience

  • Experience with hydraulic machinery

  • Experience with supervised learning or imitation learning

  • Research experience in reinforcement learning

  • Experience deploying robotic systems at scale (e.g. hundreds of units)

  • Familiarity with ROS or similar robotics frameworks

  • Experience with feature-flagged deployments, staged rollouts, or long-lived platforms

  • Experience with data curation for ML applications

  • Experience guiding, mentoring, or leading junior colleagues, students, or project teams. 

  • Familiarity with or interest in utilizing AI coding tools. 

    • This Role is a Great Fit If

  • You are passionate about building systems that work reliably in the real world

  • You want to help build a long-lived excavation planning and control system intended to scale and positively impact the entire construction industry. 

  • You are comfortable working with the realities of imperfect data and noisy measurements.

  • You have a keen interest in bridging the sim2real gap and understanding the differences between simulation and physical environments. 

  • You are excited to help drive technical direction in a growing team transitioning from prototyping to the product stage.

  • You value a collaborative team culture rooted in thoughtful design, creative thinking, mutual respect, and pragmatism.

title: Leader, EMEA Product Support
description: We are rebuilding biotech for the AI era. When a breakthrough is delayed, the world waits. Getting a molecule from discovery to patients, or a crop from lab to field, involves thousands of slow, manual, disconnected steps. AI has the potential to change this, compressing decades of R&D work into years. But that only happens when clean, structured scientific data and AI are built into how science gets done. Benchling is the AI platform for biotech R&D. Scientists use Benchling to design experiments, capture structured data, and run AI agents and models directly in their workflows. Over 200,000 scientists around the world trust Benchling to power their most important work, from academic labs to Sanofi, Moderna, and more than half of the world's top 50 biopharma. We’re building an AI scientist for our customers. We can’t do that if we haven’t built the muscle ourselves. AI fluency is the foundation we build on; it's core to how we work, and we're committed to helping every new hire integrate it into their day-to-day. As part of our interview process, you'll complete a brief AI-focused exercise or discussion so we can understand how you think about and use AI to drive impact in your role. Feel free to reference any tools, platforms, or workflows you use today. ROLE OVERVIEW The Leader, EMEA Product Support role manages Benchling support in EMEA. As the team leader (a player-coach role), you’ll manage Product Support Analalyts in Europe and spend roughly 40% of your time directly owning customer issues and our most complex escalations. This role owns live customer-impacting incidents for enterprise pharma and biotech customers, helps shape an AI-first support model, and sits close to CX leadership. Working closely with our Global Support and CX Leadership Teams, you’ll combine team leadership, incident management, and thoughtful AI adoption to help scale a modern, efficient Support organization. RESPONSIBILITIES Lead and coach your team: run daily regional support operations including prioritization and resourcing, hold regular team meetings and career growth conversations, and build a culture where people feel supported and excited to grow. Partner with the Incident Center of Excellence to mature the incident process (post-incident reviews, closing action items, communication playbooks, severity-based response criteria), and help build and run a sustainable off-hours coverage model, including personally rotating in as an escalation responder. Analyze support metrics (volume, severity trends, time-to-resolution, comms timeliness) to inform staffing and process decisions, and report trends to CX leadership. Drive consistent adoption of AI tools across support workflows, piloting ways to reduce ticket-handling time, surface account context automatically, and free up analyst time for higher-value work. Collaborate with Build, Product, Technical Account Managers, Customer Success, and Professional Services on customer issues and incidents, keep help content and product knowledge current, and represent support at customer-facing events as needed. Work the queue alongside your team: own complex, high-priority, and escalated tickets, serve as a first-line contact for regional escalations, and model the troubleshooting, investigation, and communication standards you expect from others. QUALIFICATIONS Experienced leader who coaches with empathy and stays close to the work, with 1+ years of management experience and 5+ years of SaaS support or professional services, or demonstrated leadership, including assigning ticket work and managing queues and resources. Able to personally troubleshoot and resolve complex customer issues. Working knowledge of support and incident tooling and best practices for technical support environments (e.g. Salesforce, Zendesk, JIRA, PagerDuty, or equivalent), plus genuine enthusiasm for AI in support, ideally with hands-on experience piloting or driving adoption. Sound judgment under pressure: prioritizing by urgency, severity, and customer health context, and skilled in customer-facing crisis communication, including what to say, when, and to whom during a live incident, and how to translate root cause into clear RCAs/ISNs. Experience with enterprise-grade support: managing high-stakes accounts holistically, building trust with sophisticated customers, and thinking beyond individual ticket resolution. Strong communicator and customer advocate with a bias toward action, comfortable working independently across departments, remote teams, and external stakeholders. Bachelor’s degree in a life sciences related field recommended (biology, microbiology, genetics, biotechnology, neurology, etc.); research or lab experience is a big plus. Based in the Zurich area, or willing to relocate, and able to work on-site in our Zurich office Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday. HOW WE WORK We offer a flexible hybrid work arrangement that prioritizes in-office collaboration. Employees are expected to be on-site 3 days per week (Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday). #LI-Hybrid #LI-Remote #BI-Hybrid #BI-Remote Benchling welcomes everyone. We believe diversity enriches our team so we hire people with a wide range of identities, backgrounds, and experiences. We are an equal opportunity employer. That means we don’t discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. We also consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records, consistent with applicable federal, state and local law, including but not limited to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance. We’re building an AI scientist for our customers. We can’t do that if we haven’t built the muscle ourselves. AI fluency is the foundation we build on; it's core to how we work, and we're committed to helping every new hire integrate it into their day-to-day. As part of our interview process, you'll complete a brief AI-focused exercise or discussion so we can understand how you think about and use AI to drive impact in your role. Feel free to reference any tools, platforms, or workflows you use today.

ROLE OVERVIEW

The Leader, EMEA Product Support role manages Benchling support in EMEA. As the team leader (a player-coach role), you’ll manage Product Support Analalyts in Europe and spend roughly 40% of your time directly owning customer issues and our most complex escalations. This role owns live customer-impacting incidents for enterprise pharma and biotech customers, helps shape an AI-first support model, and sits close to CX leadership. Working closely with our Global Support and CX Leadership Teams, you’ll combine team leadership, incident management, and thoughtful AI adoption to help scale a modern, efficient Support organization. 

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Lead and coach your team: run daily regional support operations including prioritization and resourcing, hold regular team meetings and career growth conversations, and build a culture where people feel supported and excited to grow.

  • Partner with the Incident Center of Excellence to mature the incident process (post-incident reviews, closing action items, communication playbooks, severity-based response criteria), and help build and run a sustainable off-hours coverage model, including personally rotating in as an escalation responder.

  • Analyze support metrics (volume, severity trends, time-to-resolution, comms timeliness) to inform staffing and process decisions, and report trends to CX leadership.

  • Drive consistent adoption of AI tools across support workflows, piloting ways to reduce ticket-handling time, surface account context automatically, and free up analyst time for higher-value work.

  • Collaborate with Build, Product, Technical Account Managers, Customer Success, and Professional Services on customer issues and incidents, keep help content and product knowledge current, and represent support at customer-facing events as needed.

  • Work the queue alongside your team: own complex, high-priority, and escalated tickets, serve as a first-line contact for regional escalations, and model the troubleshooting, investigation, and communication standards you expect from others.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experienced leader who coaches with empathy and stays close to the work, with 1+ years of management experience and 5+ years of SaaS support or professional services, or demonstrated leadership, including assigning ticket work and managing queues and resources. Able to personally troubleshoot and resolve complex customer issues.

  • Working knowledge of support and incident tooling and best practices for technical support environments (e.g. Salesforce, Zendesk, JIRA, PagerDuty, or equivalent), plus genuine enthusiasm for AI in support, ideally with hands-on experience piloting or driving adoption.

  • Sound judgment under pressure: prioritizing by urgency, severity, and customer health context, and skilled in customer-facing crisis communication, including what to say, when, and to whom during a live incident, and how to translate root cause into clear RCAs/ISNs.

  • Experience with enterprise-grade support: managing high-stakes accounts holistically, building trust with sophisticated customers, and thinking beyond individual ticket resolution.

  • Strong communicator and customer advocate with a bias toward action, comfortable working independently across departments, remote teams, and external stakeholders. Bachelor’s degree in a life sciences related field recommended (biology, microbiology, genetics, biotechnology, neurology, etc.); research or lab experience is a big plus.

  • Based in the Zurich area, or willing to relocate, and able to work on-site in our Zurich office Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday.

     

HOW WE WORK

We offer a flexible hybrid work arrangement that prioritizes in-office collaboration. Employees are expected to be on-site 3 days per week (Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday).

raw.title: Sentinel System Engineer - Post Launch Support
raw.description:
We are looking for a Sentinel System Engineer on behalf of the European Space Agency (ESA) for their location in Noordwijk, the Netherlands. 

 

Please note, the successful candidate will be employed by ATG Europe (or one of its subsidiaries). Furthermore, upon selection, they will be subject to a general security screening performed by an external provider (further information will be provided at the interview stage). 

 

ATG is dedicated to diversity and inclusion and is an equal opportunity employer. Regardless of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, or any other reason protected by relevant state or municipal legislation, we are pleased to consider all eligible candidates for employment. 

 

The successful candidate will be tasked with, but not limited to: 

 

  • Coordinate the internal & external support to PLS (ESA Space Segment Development Team, TEC experts, Mission Analysis & System Support, Industry);  

  • Coordinate with the ESA Space Segment Development Team (where relevant) to exchange technical status on the flying- and non-flying satellite(s), identifying coordination issues of relevance and following them to conclusion;  

  • Support PLS at the regular (weekly) Operations Boards; 

  • Support the Operations Team(s) by providing or facilitating responses to technical support requests from either the Flight Operations Segment (FOS) or Payload Data Ground Segment (PDGS);  

  • Maintain & distribute the PLS On-Call lists to the FOS (& other parties where relevant) in a timely manner; 

  • Support the Mission Manager and his/her team by providing technical advice related to issues of Satellite(s) performance; 

  • Support the Space Segment Development Team(s) by providing timely & pertinent feedback on any issue detected in-flight with potential impact on satellite(s) still under development;  

  • Provide specific technical expertise to support Performance Monitoring, Analysis & Optimisation tasks and Anomaly Investigations, with overall aim to improve mission quality and/or lifetime; 

  • Preparation of Technical Documentation, such as Reports, Technical Notes and other requested documentation; 

  • Review and synthesis of Technical Reports and documents produced by Industry, and extraction of relevant technical information for use in generation of PLS Performance metrics and reports; 

  • Organise and support the 6-monthly Satellite In-Orbit Performance (SIOP) Technical Meetings in cooperation with the Industrial Prime contractor, including associated follow-up activities (eg. administration, actions follow up etc); 

  • Respond to Anomaly Warnings received from the Flight Operations Segment (FOS) in an appropriate & timely manner, providing support and facilitating the necessary follow-on actions;  

  • Support and lead complex investigations that arise as a result of satellite performance and anomalies, ensuring adequate coordination with involved partners (Mission Management, Operations Team(s), Industry, Space Segment Development Team(s), Management);   

  • Prepare, coordinate & follow-up on engineering requests for the Industrial contractors in support of Anomaly Investigations and other technical analyses;   

  • Support satellite configuration control including the Configuration Control Board (CCB);   

  • Support Satellite Decommissioning & Disposal activities as required;   

  • Monitor, track and report the status of activities performed by the Industrial contractors in support of the PLS function (technical, commercial and schedule status);  

  • Review commercial payment requests & the associated justifications submitted by Industry (regular milestones or as result of ad-hoc Cost Reimbursement activities);   

  • Bring innovation to satellite performance analysis by investigating emerging technologies that enhance the ability for early detection of performance trends and deviations;   

  • Maintain the relevant PLS technical records, databases & documentation in accordance with established procedures;   

  • Maintain a regular reporting in coordination with the Technical Officer. 


Please ensure that your CV clearly explains how you meet the mandatory requirements. If it doesn’t align completely with the essential criteria, it could result in rejection. 

Requirements  

  • University degree in a relevant Engineering discipline;   

  • Minimum 10 years of experience and a significant background in one or more of the following domains: Satellite Operations, Spacecraft Development (including Project Engineering, Equipment/Subsystem Procurement, Assembly Integration & Test);   

  • Minimum 3 years’ experience working as a System Engineer or with a System Coordination function in any of the above domains;   

  • Good understanding of the Satellite Phase E2 Routine Operations Organisation and the typical activities performed;   

  • Good understanding of the factors affecting the short- and long-term performance of Satellites and their main subsystems or payloads;   

  • Experience managing and leading technical meetings and discussions with multiple stakeholders;

  • Proven experience & ability at working in an environment with multiple external interfaces;   

  • Good at working in a team and a proactive attitude to solving problems  

  • Autonomy in writing technical notes, specifications and reports in English;   

  • Good interpersonal skills and team spirit;   

  • Demonstrable multidisciplinary or system-level experience in the satellite engineering domain;  

  • Previous working experience in a multinational environment is desirable;  

  • Very good knowledge of MS Office tools; 

  • Fluency in English, both written and spoken; 

  • Candidates must be eligible to work in the EU. 

 

Please submit your application in English via the apply button below. Applications submitted in other languages will not be considered.
